description: An object holding a zero-based page number, a page size and a Sort that Spring Data applies as ORDER BY, limit and offset.
Page carries totals and may need a COUNT query, which Spring Data can skip when the result reveals the total; Slice only tracks whether another slice exists.
An ordering with a unique tie-breaker that is deterministic for an unchanged result set; concurrent changes can still shift rows between offset pages.
A fixed set of property names a client may sort by, checked in the service because request values are not validated against the model.
Fetching the rows after the last seen sort key instead of skipping an offset, exposed in Spring Data as Window and ScrollPosition.
The effect that the database reads and discards every row before the offset, so deep pages are slower than early ones.
An application-owned record with content and page metadata, returned instead of Spring Data's Page so the JSON stays stable.
